# BitChord 1.0.0
## Highlights
- Build phrase-aware AutoMix transitions with beat-matched tempo changes and varied effects. - Choose a lyrics source per track, translate lyrics, and share lyric cards with word timing. - Watch music videos with Picture in Picture and a full-screen theater. - Import Spotify playlists, organize local music, and manage downloads in batches. - Open search results and library shelves in separate Mac windows. - Use the new iPhone and iPad player layouts, including the two-pane iPad player.
## Playback and AutoMix
- Blend tracks on measured bars, phrases, clean instrumental outros, and detected vocal cues. - Glide tempo to match the incoming track and fall back to a clean crossfade when a match is unsuitable. - Add Echo Out, loop roll, reverb wash, brake, texture, and cut-on-the-one transitions. - Keep loudness matched as the next track comes in, with gains prepared before the blend. - Use beat and downbeat analysis from the optional Beat This! model or the built-in fallback; the bundled vocal model keeps transitions off vocals. - Keep analysis results across launches and sequence long collections with a rolling queue window. - Mix on a manual skip when the setting is enabled. - Adapt playback quality to audio routes and metered connections, and hear audio without a separate stream probe.
## Lyrics
- Choose a provider for an individual track and see providers race with live status. - Remember provider choices per song, with cross-device sync in builds signed with the required iCloud capabilities. - Translate lyrics, follow the app language by default, and read language names in English. - Share lyric cards with original and translated text, selected passages, and adjustable quote lengths. - Read right-to-left lyrics and lyric strips in the correct direction. - See word timing assembled from timed syllables, and identify BitChord-supplied timing. - Export story-sized lyric cards. - Find lyric sources that support synced lyrics and manage providers from the player.
## Video
- Find music videos through YouTube Music's own song-to-video link, then search official music videos when no counterpart is available. - Keep lyric uploads and other user-generated videos out of automatic picks; use the artwork fallback when no suitable video is found. - Watch video in Picture in Picture or a full-screen theater with playback and seek controls. - Align the picture to the song with piecewise timing and confidence checks; fall back to artwork when alignment is uncertain. - See the selected video over its own audio or over the song's audio, depending on the match. - Choose whether music video playback may use cellular data.
## Library and downloads
- Browse local albums and artists, with albums ordered by their tagged track numbers. - Find downloaded songs and collections from the On Device library. - Select and remove multiple downloads together, and manage cached songs from Settings. - Upload selected local or downloaded tracks to WebDAV. - Import Spotify playlists by link, including playlists with more than 100 tracks; imported playlists keep their order and artwork. - Save playlists on the device without signing in, and manage playlists from their cards and menus.
## Search and browse
- Search songs, albums, artists, playlists, and configured add-on sources. - See live typeahead suggestions, keep recent searches, and filter results by media type. - Page through results and stop cleanly when a source has no further progress. - Browse category shelves, artist pages, top songs, latest releases, and expanded grids. - Open a search or shelf in its own Mac window and continue browsing there.
## Mac
- Navigate with a playlist-aware sidebar, unified Settings window, and window-level account controls. - Open search results, browse pages, and library shelves in separate windows. - Use a compact player in the menu bar, a floating Mini Player, and Dock playback controls. - Play and select tracks with arrow keys and Return, and move between lyrics and queue in the inspector. - Control playback and reach track actions from the menu bar and keyboard menus.
## iPhone and iPad
- Use updated Liquid Glass controls, Dynamic Type layouts, and the system playback pill. - Pull up the playback pill to open Now Playing, or long-press to see the next track. - Put lyrics or the queue beside the player artwork in the iPad two-pane layout. - Continue playback at the live position through device handoff. - Use Siri, Shortcuts, and Spotlight to play, search, like, and queue music.
## Accounts and sync
- Review an account profile before saving a YouTube Music sign-in, and switch among available channels in Settings. - See clearer sign-in and search errors, and keep local playlists available while signed out. - Share a validated YouTube Music session through iCloud Keychain, with an explicit adoption choice on another device. - iCloud lyrics-choice and sign-in sharing work in builds signed with the required iCloud capabilities; unsigned packages and builds without those capabilities use local storage.
## Settings
- Search for individual settings and navigate Settings with back and forward controls on Mac. - Configure playback, audio quality, AutoMix, video, downloads, lyrics, local libraries, and scrobbling. - Choose Mix on Skip and control whether video may use cellular data.
## Performance
- Stop canvas sampling and downloads when their view is inactive, avoid decoding a canvas behind music video, and cancel shared downloads when no view is waiting. - Pause playback-position timelines while transport is paused and bound decoded blur artwork in memory. - Limit speculative stream URL requests on metered connections and remember empty artist lookups across launches. - Reuse mixer buffers, reduce diagnostic work, and allow unrelated AutoMix analyses to proceed independently.
## Fixes
- Resume playback and downloads more reliably after pauses, failures, network changes, and interrupted loads. - Keep search and browse continuation state when a page arrives late or makes no progress. - Keep account refusal and provider access errors visible instead of leaving screens in a loading state. - Preserve selected artwork, playlist order, and local library tags during imports. - Keep the player's queue, handoff position, lyric selection, and track identity in sync as playback changes. - Avoid repeated update prompts after acknowledging a release.
## Requirements
- macOS 15 or later on Apple Silicon. - iOS or iPadOS 18 or later.
## Downloads and installation
- **Mac:** Apple Silicon DMG. It is ad-hoc signed, not notarized, and not Developer ID signed. - **iOS:** Unsigned IPA for sideloading with AltStore, SideStore, or Sideloadly, or for signing with your own Apple Developer team.
### Install on Mac
Drag BitChord to Applications, then open it. If Gatekeeper blocks the first launch, use either route:
- **System Settings:** Open System Settings → Privacy & Security, scroll to Security, choose **Open Anyway** for BitChord, then confirm **Open** in the warning dialog. - **Terminal:** After moving BitChord to Applications, run:
```sh xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine "/Applications/BitChord.app" open "/Applications/BitChord.app" ```
### Sideload on iPhone or iPad
1. Install AltStore, SideStore, or Sideloadly and connect the device as required by that tool. 2. Import the unsigned IPA and sign it with your Apple account or developer team. 3. Install the signed app and trust the developer profile if iOS asks.
To use iCloud lyrics-choice or sign-in sharing, sign the app with your own team and enable the matching iCloud Key-Value Store and iCloud Keychain capabilities and provisioning profile. Otherwise those features use local device storage.
## Legal
BitChord does not host or provide media. Playback uses configured third-party services and their APIs; availability and terms are controlled by those services. See the [README Disclaimer & Legal Notice](https://github.com/bagumamartin/BitChord/blob/v1.0.0/README.md#disclaimer--legal-notice).
Every GitHub release is built from its tagged commit, and that tag's source archive is the Corresponding Source under GPLv3 §6. The source for this release is the [v1.0.0 tag](https://github.com/bagumamartin/BitChord/tree/v1.0.0).

### What's changed - Update notices now remember when you've acted on a release, so the same version won't keep appearing. A newer release will still be announced. - On iPhone and iPad, choosing either alert action acknowledges that release. On Mac, Sparkle remembers your choice.
### macOS build Apple Silicon (arm64). The app is ad-hoc signed and the build is not notarized, so macOS may block the first launch.
### Opening BitChord on macOS Only continue if you downloaded this DMG from the official BitChord release and trust it.
**System Settings:** Move BitChord to Applications and try to open it once. If macOS blocks it, open System Settings → Privacy & Security, scroll to Security, choose **Open Anyway** for BitChord, then confirm **Open** in the warning dialog.
**Terminal:** After moving BitChord to Applications, open Terminal and run: ```sh xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine "/Applications/BitChord.app" open "/Applications/BitChord.app" ``` This removes the downloaded-file quarantine attribute from the app bundle so Gatekeeper no longer blocks this launch.

### What's changed - Recommendation queues now refresh on deliberate listening actions and refill only when fewer than three tracks remain, keeping natural song transitions steady. - Removing tracks from the queue no longer triggers an immediate refresh; Automix can still reorder queued tracks. - Google sign-in follows Google's own flow without BitChord intercepting password or passkey steps. - The macOS sidebar toggle stays visible, Recents loading layouts adapt to larger screens, and closing Now Playing returns to the same screen and position.
### macOS download This Apple Silicon build is ad-hoc signed and is not notarized by Apple. macOS may block its first launch.
Only continue if you downloaded BitChord from the official BitChord GitHub release and trust it.
**System Settings:** Move BitChord to Applications and try to open it once. If macOS blocks it, open System Settings → Privacy & Security, scroll to Security, choose **Open Anyway** for BitChord, then confirm **Open** in the warning dialog.
**Terminal:** After moving BitChord to Applications, open Terminal and run: ```sh xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine "/Applications/BitChord.app" open "/Applications/BitChord.app" ``` This removes the downloaded-file quarantine attribute from the app bundle so Gatekeeper no longer blocks this launch.
